From 67b53a660e6bf0da2fa8d8872e897a14d8059eaf Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wenkai Lin <linwenkai6@hisilicon.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 15:00:38 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: hisilicon/sec2 - prevent req used-after-free for sec

During packet transmission, if the system is under heavy load,
the hardware might complete processing the packet and free the
request memory (req) before the transmission function finishes.
If the software subsequently accesses this req, a use-after-free
error will occur. The qp_ctx memory exists throughout the packet
sending process, so replace the req with the qp_ctx.

Fixes: f0ae287c5045 ("crypto: hisilicon/sec2 - implement full backlog mode for sec")
Signed-off-by: Wenkai Lin <linwenkai6@hisilicon.com>
Signed-off-by: Chenghai Huang <huangchenghai2@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

diff --git a/drivers/crypto/hisilicon/sec2/sec_crypto.c b/drivers/crypto/hisilicon/sec2/sec_crypto.c
index 15174216d8c4..2471a4dd0b50 100644
--- a/drivers/crypto/hisilicon/sec2/sec_crypto.c
+++ b/drivers/crypto/hisilicon/sec2/sec_crypto.c
@@ -230,7 +230,7 @@ static int qp_send_message(struct sec_req *req)
 
 	spin_unlock_bh(&qp_ctx->req_lock);
 
-	atomic64_inc(&req->ctx->sec->debug.dfx.send_cnt);
+	atomic64_inc(&qp_ctx->ctx->sec->debug.dfx.send_cnt);
 	return -EINPROGRESS;
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in the Hisilicon SEC2 crypto driver by replacing a pointer to a request that may be freed with a pointer to a context that remains valid throughout the packet transmission.

### Modifications per File

- **`drivers/crypto/hisilicon/sec2/sec_crypto.c`**  
  In function `qp_send_message`, one line is changed:  
  - `atomic64_inc(&req->ctx->sec->debug.dfx.send_cnt);` → `atomic64_inc(&qp_ctx->ctx->sec->debug.dfx.send_cnt);`  
  The access to `req->ctx` is replaced with `qp_ctx->ctx`, where `qp_ctx` is a per‑queue context whose lifetime extends across the entire send operation.

### Relationship Between Changes

The fix addresses a race condition: under heavy load, the hardware may complete processing and free the request (`req`) before the software finishes executing `qp_send_message`. Directly accessing `req->ctx` after that point leads to use‑after‑free. By using `qp_ctx` (which persists until the queue is destroyed), the driver safely reaches the same `ctx->sec->debug.dfx.send_cnt` counter without relying on the freed `req`.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
atomic64_inc(&req->ctx->sec->debug.dfx.send_cnt);
Reason:
After `hisi_qp_send` is called, the hardware may complete the request and free the `req` memory asynchronously before the subsequent `atomic64_inc` accesses `req->ctx`, causing a use-after-free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
atomic64_inc(&qp_ctx->ctx->sec->debug.dfx.send_cnt);
Reason:
`qp_ctx` is allocated per queue and remains valid throughout the entire packet transmission process, so accessing `qp_ctx->ctx` instead of `req->ctx` avoids dereferencing a potentially freed request.
